title: Soft Are the Fruitful Showers That Bring
description: Soft Are the Fruitful Showers That Bring in Tonic Solfa to HOLY MATRIMONY, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Moore wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 336 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Pardon”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Particular Metre (8.8.6.8.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HOLY MATRIMONY; any other Common Particular Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Soft are the fruit-ful showers that bring The wel-come pro-mise of the spring, And soft the ver-nal gale: Sweet the wild war-blings of the grove, The voice of na-ture and of love, That glad-den ev-ery vale.

lines: Soft are the fruitful showers that bring
The welcome promise of the spring,
And soft the vernal gale:
Sweet the wild warblings of the grove,
The voice of nature and of love,
That gladden every vale.
But softer in the mourner's ear
Sounds the mild voice of mercy near,
That whispers sins forgiven;
And sweeter far the music swells,
When to the raptured soul she tells
Of peace and promised heaven.
Fair are the flowers that deck the ground;
And groves and gardens blooming round,
Unnumbered charms unfold:
Bright is the sun's meridian ray,
And bright the beams of setting day,
That robe the clouds in gold.
But far more fair the pious breast,
In richer robes of goodness dressed,
Where heaven's own graces shine;
And brighter far the prospects rise,
That burst on faith's delighted eyes,
From glories all divine.

licence: Public domain: Henry Moore died in 1802.
credits: Words by Henry Moore (1732–1802), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to HOLY MATRIMONY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
